messages:
jessica-support: Heads-up — Enterprise customer KeyWave reporting EU users seeing +300-600ms token latency spikes and intermittent 401s. They say traffic is landing in us-east even though their DNS resolves to eu-west. Escalating for triage.

caroline-cs: Billing shows repeated retries from the same request IDs, cost spike. They noticed this started after our DNS mapping push around 12:30 UTC. Customer is pretty nervous.

mike-eng: Can we get a small repro (dig + traceroute + a sample request id)? Also want their resolver IP and EDNS info (if present).

jessica-support: Pasted what they sent:
```
# dig +short A api.redwood.example.com @8.26.14.2
3.12.45.67

# traceroute to 3.12.45.67
 1  10.0.0.1
 2  192.0.2.1
 3  52.95.120.1
 4  3.12.45.67

Request-ID: req_20260315_abc123
Headers: no EDNS, client-ip=203.0.113.54
```

oliver-netops: That resolver (8.26.14.2) is ISPWave and looks like it's returning a cached A pointing at our us-east pop (3.12.45.67). Our recent change lowered eu-west TTL to 60s, but some resolvers prefetch and ignore short TTLs or strip EDNS so geo-lookup falls back to older mapping.

mike-eng: Two quick mitigations: 1) Ask customer/ISP to flush resolver caches or use a public resolver (1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8) to confirm. 2) Ops can add a short-lived eu-specific alias (CNAME) with a 120s TTL to force re-resolve on their path. Also we should verify our geoip DB entry for that ASN/cidr.

jessica-support: Customer tried local DNS flush and browser clear, still hitting us-east. They provided ISP resolver 8.26.14.2 and said ISPWave is their upstream.

oliver-netops: I see two contributing factors: (a) resolver kept the old A for longer than TTL due to prefetch behavior; (b) request lacked EDNS-client-subnet so our edge couldn't infer geoip reliably and fallback routing picked the default region.

mike-eng: Agreed. For short-term rollback-safe fix, we'll create an alias 'api-eu-tail' -> eu pool with 120s TTL and announce to affected customers to change the host in their test request. This avoids immediate mass CNAME change but forces the resolver to get the eu answer. I'll also open a ticket to check EDNS stripping for ISPWave.

infra-bot: deploy-dns-change: initiated dns update dns-2026-03-15-42 (create cname api-eu-tail.redwood.example.com -> eu-pop-01.redwood.net, ttl=120). Expected propagation 2-5m.

mike-eng: Additionally adding a temporary routing preference: prefer eu-pop if Country header or X-Client-Country indicates GB/DE/FR/etc. Won't affect clients that send no country info but helps most web clients.

caroline-cs: Told customer: test with curl forced-resolve and with 1.1.1.1 and report back. Gave them this command:
```
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:54.93.11.22 'https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health'
# or use dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.example.com +short
```

jessica-support: Customer reports: after ~4 minutes of the dns change they now resolve to eu-pop and latency/goes back to normal, 401s stopped. They will monitor for 48h.

oliver-netops: We'll keep the alias live for 6h, then revert to normal names once caches look healthy. Follow-up actions: 1) confirm geoip DB entry for ISPWave ASN, 2) add note to release docs about resolver prefetch risk, 3) consider lowering TTL ramp strategy next time.

mike-eng: I'll open the infra ticket and put a short postmortem on the incident board.

jessica-support: Closing loop with customer and noting contact for ISPWave. Thanks all :thumbsup:
